newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end higher in last-minute revival.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end higher in last-minute revival.

text.p: The Manila stock index recovered in the last few trades of the day on Friday, ending up 0.88 points, or 0.03 percent, at 3,131.14 points.
The index, dragged down earlier by Ayala Land, recovered dramatically when one brokerage bought up the real estate heavyweight in the last few minutes, brokers said.
"One of the local brokers bought up the stock. They were propping it up," one broker said.
Ayala Land ended the day at 30 pesos, unchanged from the previous close. At mid-session, it touched a low of 28 pesos, which took the main index down by one percent to 3,130 points.
Brokers said foreign funds had sold off Ayala Land because it had a high price-earnings ratio and on fears Manila property prices were falling from their peak.
Except for property shares which were down, all others were either steady or had gained. Heavyweight San Miguel gained on Friday's news of lower inflation, brokers said.
The government announced that inflation in September had fallen to 4.4 percent, the lowest level in nine years.
Inflation was at 7.9 percent last month and 11.3 percent in September, 1995.
"Lower inflation means more disposable incomes and more purchasing power," said Noel Reyes of Anscor Hagedorn Securities, adding that San Miguel beer would benefit.
The overall market, however, continued to lack direction as investors awaited fresh incentives, Patrick Garcia of brokerage L.M. Garcia & Associates said.
The lower inflation figures were already factored in by the market, he said. - UDAY KHANDEPARKAR (632) 841 8934
